name: Idiopathic Steroid-Resistant Nephrotic Syndrome with Sensitivity to Second-Line Immunosuppressive Therapy
aliases: Steroid-Resistant Nephrotic Syndrome (SRNS) with Immunosuppressive Responsiveness
Idiopathic SRNS Responsive to Second-Line Agents

criteria.description: Persistent nephrotic-range proteinuria despite standard corticosteroid therapy for at least 4 weeks
Renal biopsy showing minimal change disease, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, or mesangial proliferation without secondary causes
Exclusion of secondary causes of nephrotic syndrome such as infections, systemic diseases, or genetic mutations known to cause SRNS
Demonstrated clinical remission or partial remission with second-line immunosuppressive agents (e.g., calcineurin inhibitors, cyclophosphamide)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent nephrotic-range proteinuria despite corticosteroids, characteristic renal biopsy findings, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be performed to exclude monogenic causes of steroid resistance.

pathognomonic.notes: Due to hypoalbuminemia and fluid retention

common.notes: Mild to moderate elevation in blood pressure
Secondary to protein loss and edema
Occasional presence of red blood cells in urine

occasional.notes: Abdominal fluid accumulation secondary to hypoalbuminemia

searchTerms: infections due to weak immune system

rare.notes: Chronic disease and steroid exposure effects

laboratory: Normal or elevated serum creatinine depending on disease progression
Negative serologies for secondary causes (e.g., ANA, complement levels normal)
imaging: Renal ultrasound typically normal or shows increased echogenicity
Chest X-ray may show pleural effusions in advanced cases
genetic: Genetic testing to exclude mutations in NPHS1, NPHS2, WT1, and other SRNS-associated genes
other: Renal biopsy showing minimal change disease, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, or mesangial proliferation
Response to second-line immunosuppressive therapy (e.g., calcineurin inhibitors)

distinguishingFeatures: Onset in first 3 months of life
Associated with systemic diseases (e.g., lupus nephritis, infections)
Positive serologic markers for underlying disease
Histologic findings consistent with secondary causes

redFlags: Persistent nephrotic syndrome despite second-line immunosuppressive therapy
references: International Pediatric Nephrology Association Guidelines on Steroid-Resistant Nephrotic Syndrome, 2024
Orphanet Report on Idiopathic Steroid-Resistant Nephrotic Syndrome (ORPHA:567552)
Journal of the American Society of Nephrology, 2023: Advances in SRNS Management
